vectors.title: Birth with a full date, person alive: day and month removed
Birth with a full date, person deceased: the same (living or deceased)
Adult Christening 14 is birth-like
Baptism 15 of a deceased person is birth-like
Bless 18 is birth-like
Christen 22 is birth-like
Stillbirth 45 is birth-like
Custom event types: the birth pattern is a case-insensitive substring match; other custom types keep their dates
Death, Marriage, Burial and Residence are not birth-like: their dates are stored whole
An event at a person's birth_ref_index is birth-like whatever its type (a Birth retyped to Residence)
A birth_ref_index of -1 or beyond the list points at nothing: no event becomes birth-like
An event shared by two persons is birth-like when any person has it at birth_ref_index
A Birth event no person references is still birth-like by its type
RANGE: the second day and month (dateval 4 and 5) go too
SPAN: the second day and month go too, the modifier stays
RANGE with a day in the second half only is still refused
TEXTONLY: becomes a plain date with the first four-digit year of its text
TEXTONLY with no four-digit year becomes an empty date
TEXTONLY whose text is a bare year passes the text check but is still refused as TEXTONLY
The text of a plain date is cleared; the server refuses any text other than a bare year
ABOUT with a full date: the modifier and quality stay, day and month go
BEFORE with a month and no day: the month goes
A dual-year (slash) date keeps its flag
A Julian date is reduced with the Julian day number of January 1
A date in another calendar gets sortval 0
Day and month with no year: reduced to an empty date
A year-only date is already reduced and does not change
A citation of a birth-like event loses its day and month; a citation of a death keeps its date
A citation reached only through the EventRef of a birth-like event is reduced too, text included
A citation of a marriage keeps its date
The date of a name of type Birth loses day, month and text; a married name or an AKA keeps its date
Any Date of any class equal to a local full birth date is reduced: event, citation, media, married name; a date one day off is kept
A family event on a date that is some person's birth date is reduced (other people's objects included)
An event that was birth-like at a synced base keeps day and month local after a retype, until io releases it
AGE, FATHER_AGE, MOTHER_AGE and TIME attributes are local-only on persons, events and event references
The whole LDS ordinance list is local-only
